title: The Biscuit Negotiator
context: Four panels show a recurring stick-figure person and a small dog. Affection leads to suspicion that the dog is manipulating the person into giving treats; the dog appears pleased that the tactic works. Bubble wording is inspiration, not a script to read aloud.

characters.name: Person
characters.description: A recurring stick figure interacting with the dog.
characters.observed_traits: Simple stick figure. Human age and gender are not visually established.
characters.personality: Fictional: loving, observant and determined to establish boundaries, but easily disarmed by warmth.
characters.voice_direction: Warm conversational voice; dry comic timing; suspicion softens into affection.

characters.name: Dog
characters.observed_traits: Four-legged animal with floppy ears and a wagging tail in one panel.
characters.personality: Fictional: an affectionate little strategist who treats every biscuit as a diplomatic negotiation.
characters.voice_direction: Bright, nimble, playful character voice; charming confidence with small pauses before punchlines.

lines.text: You arranged my slippers in a heart. What did you break?
lines.direction: Quiet suspicion; hold the last question for a beat.

lines.text: Nothing. I am celebrating your excellent taste in companions.
lines.direction: Earnest flattery; warm and almost excessively polite.

lines.text: The biscuit cupboard is behind me, isn't it?
lines.direction: Dry realization, slowing down on biscuit cupboard.

lines.text: That is an unfortunate coincidence. Now, about my performance review.
lines.direction: Brief hesitation, then recover into businesslike confidence.
Matter of fact; let the accusation land.

lines.text: I was protecting the house from unnecessary visitors.
lines.direction: Prompt, proud reply as if the logic is impeccable.
Sharper, but still playful; short and clipped.
Gentle smugness; leave a small comic beat between sentences.

lines.text: One biscuit. And one honest answer. Would you still love me without them?
lines.direction: The joke falls away; sincere, softer, unhurried.

lines.text: But I would write a strongly worded letter.
lines.direction: Soft, conspiratorial finish; smile in the voice.
Warm affection with a small amused breath.

warnings: Handwritten example of an original directed story; not a live model result.
synopsis: A dog tries to turn household affection into a formal treat contract. The person catches on, but discovers that the affection is real too.
